subject: Unusual AWS Marketplace credits on April invoice — ledger alignment request
messages:
From: Tanya Singh <tanya.singh@acme-corp.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: billing@acme-corp.com
Date: 2029-04-11T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Unexpected negative credits on Apr AWS marketplace invoice

Hi Olga / Marissa,

We're reconciling the April AWS Marketplace invoice and noticed several negative line items (credits) that don't map to any of the support credits we've requested. The invoice shows ~USD 14,800 credited against our usage for April 1–10, but our internal ledger shows steady usage with no refunds requested. Can you: 

- Confirm whether Redwood issued any retroactive credits on AWS's side for ACME's account during that window
- Share transaction IDs or metering IDs that caused the settlement credit

I've attached our exported invoice and a short list of the credit line item IDs as they appear in AWS. This is blocking our internal month-end close — appreciate a quick triage.

Thanks,
Tanya Singh
Head of Finance, Acme Analytics
(t) +1 415-555-0199

Attachments: acme_apr_marketplace_invoice_20290401.csv, metering_ids_sample.txt
From: olga.petrov@redwood.com <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Tanya Singh <tanya.singh@acme-corp.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2029-04-11T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected negative credits on Apr AWS marketplace invoice

Hi Tanya — thanks for flagging this.

Quick update: we haven't proactively issued any customer-facing refunds for ACME in April. The likely causes are: a) an AWS-side reconciliation adjustment applied by the marketplace which shows as a credit, or b) a retro-billing correction from an earlier metering batch. I'm looping in Karthik from Marketplace Billing (cc) to pull the subledger snapshot and the raw metering IDs.

Next steps for us: 
- Karthik to pull Redwood's subledger for ACME and the kernel of marketplace transaction mappings (today EOD).
- I'll open a ticket with AWS Marketplace support if internal alignment doesn't find a mapping.
- We'll return a CSV that maps AWS transaction IDs -> Redwood subledger lines so you can reconcile on your side.

Can you confirm the HubSpot invoice reference you used (hs id) so we send the matching internal file?

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Finance Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, Tanya Singh <tanya.singh@acme-corp.com>
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.com
Date: 2029-04-11T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected negative credits on Apr AWS marketplace invoice

Hi all,

I pulled the subledger snapshot and did a quick join against the metering IDs Tanya shared. Attached is a slice of the ledger showing the three credit events (lines highlighted). Preliminary notes: 

- Two credits (tx 0x7f3a, 0x8b21) are marketplace reversals linked to a SKU remap on 2029-03-27 affecting a small spike of synthetic test traffic we had routed to ACME's staging listing. We applied an intercompany offset that should have been internal — looks like it was routed to the external settlement by mistake.
- The third credit (tx 0x9c14) is an AWS platform-initiated settlement correction tied to a late usage correction from Feb. That one originates on AWS' end.

I've attached: redwood_subledger_snapshot_20290410.csv (filtered) and a short mapping file. Action items: 
1) Olga — can you confirm whether we should request AWS to reverse the platform correction or produce a memo to ACME to accept the credit?
2) Jordan — please prepare a short note for ACME that explains the internal routing error and the remediation plan.

I'll keep digging into the staging traffic attribution to make sure the intercompany offset doesn't recur.

Karthik
Marketplace Billing Lead
From: olga.petrov@redwood.com <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Tanya Singh <tanya.singh@acme-corp.com>, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Date: 2029-04-11T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected negative credits on Apr AWS marketplace invoice

Tanya — thanks for your patience. Karthik's analysis attached explains the three credit lines: two caused by an internal routing mistake on our side and one is an AWS platform correction. Our proposed remediation: 

- For the two internal routing credits: we'll issue an offsetting charge via our next monthly settlement and provide a short supporting memo that you can attach to ACME's books. That avoids a retro-charge on ACME's card and keeps collection simple.
- For the AWS platform correction: we'll open a support case asking AWS to provide their settlement rationale and supporting metering IDs. If AWS reverses, we'll pass that through; if not, we will show it as an external platform adjustment and provide evidence.

Requested from ACME: please confirm you prefer an internal offset (Redwood issues a compensating charge) or that you'd rather we request AWS to reverse the platform correction. If you prefer the latter, we'll escalate the AWS case and keep you copied.

I'll draft the memo and the offset invoice tonight and share for approval.

Best,
Olga
From: Tanya Singh <tanya.singh@acme-corp.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: billing@acme-corp.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Date: 2029-04-12T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected negative credits on Apr AWS marketplace invoice

Hi Olga / Karthik — appreciate the quick turnaround and the clear options. ACME prefers Redwood to issue the internal offset (compensating charge) plus the memo; that minimizes our accounting churn and keeps AR clean. Please proceed with the offset invoice and include the subledger mapping in the memo. If AWS later reverses the platform correction, we can reconcile then.

A couple of quick asks: 
- Please include both Redwood and AWS transaction IDs in the memo so our auditors have a single reconciliation file.
- Could you add our HubSpot invoice ref: hs_884211_ACME to the memo filename?

Thanks — looking forward to the memo and offset invoice.

Best,
Tanya
Head of Finance, Acme Analytics
